Messages.Author: Scott Halvorson
Messages.Body:
Reading the newsgroups and playing with friends have raised a few
questions that I need to know the answers to, also to explain a few
rulings to my gaming group.

1) What is the official ruling on vampires performing the same action
twice in a turn? I thought that it can't be done, but someone else has
said that it depends on the cards played. For example, a vampire bleeds
me with Social Charms, and I block it. During combat, he plays Majesty
to end combat and untap. Then he wants to bleed me with the same
vampire using Govern the Unaligned. I say that he can't perform a
second bleed action. He says that he is using a different card do
bleed, so it is allowed. What is the ruling? Also, along these lines,
Why is Obedience printed the way it is (vampire may not perform this
action again) if the way I think the rule is is correct? Same for
Rutor's Hand; will it allow a tapped vampire who bled earlier to bleed
again?

2) Is the Crimson Sentinel banned?

3) If I understand the stikes discussion correctly, if Basilia is
equipped with Tiger Claws, in combat she can either strike her opponent
for 3 normal damage or 1 ag damage. The Tiger Claws is a melee weapon
strike, not a boost to her hand strike, thus she does not have 3 ag
damage. Is this correct? Why was this ruling made, if correct?

4) Camille Devereux had a name change to Raven in the V:tES reprint.
She also apparently had a face lift (aka new artwork). Can I have one
of each of these cards in play uncontested, or do they contest each
other?

5) I don't understand the M1kF discussion about requirement vs.
restriction. How does the Inner Circle member using M1kF to take over
the Atonement action result? What are some other examples to clarify
requirement vs. restriction?

6) Why would the Leather Jacket not prevent the damage done by a
vampire playing Burst of Sunlight? The Jacket prevents damage done from
a strike, but it doesn't necessarily have to be your opponent's strike,
does it? Same for Body of Sun at basic level - both vampires take 3 or
1 ag damage, depending on range. The Jacket could be used to prevent
that damage as well, couldn't it?

7) Where can I find the FAQs and rulings lists? I've tried searching
dejanews, but I haven't had much luck.

Scott Halvorson
halv...@cptc.wisc.edu

Messages.Author: ber...@cco.caltech.edu
Messages.Body:
> 1) What is the official ruling on vampires performing the same action
> twice in a turn? I thought that it can't be done, but someone else has
> said that it depends on the cards played. For example, a vampire bleeds
> me with Social Charms, and I block it. During combat, he plays Majesty
> to end combat and untap. Then he wants to bleed me with the same
> vampire using Govern the Unaligned. I say that he can't perform a
> second bleed action. He says that he is using a different card do
> bleed, so it is allowed. What is the ruling? Also, along these lines,
> Why is Obedience printed the way it is (vampire may not perform this
> action again) if the way I think the rule is is correct? Same for
> Rutor's Hand; will it allow a tapped vampire who bled earlier to bleed
> again?
>

Well, No Repeat Actions (NRA), is essentially a tournament rule. That
is, it is enforced in all tournaments. Many playgroups use NRA as a
house rule because there are a number of repeated action combos that are
very broken. (See bleed/Day Op/Movement of the Slowed Body(or Freak
Drive)/Rapid Healing/Force of Will/lather/rinse/repeat) However, if you
are using NRA (which IMHO you should be), it goes something like this:

There are certain action types defined in the rule book. These are (I
think):

Bleed (either with a card, or the cardless (D)bleed prey) Hunt Recruit
Ally Employ Retainer Equip Political Action Leave Torpor (either with a
card, or the cardless +1 stealth: leave torpor) Rescue from Torpor
Diablerize

I think those are all. Now, there are essentially two rules in NRA. 1) If
an action a minion takes falls into one of these categories, that minion
may not take any other action in that category this turn. 2) A minion may
not play the same action card from your hand more than once a turn.

So, let's say a minion bleeds with Govern the Unaligned. That minion may
not bleed again this turn, and it may not play Govern the Unaligned this
turn.

Say, instead, that a minion uses sup. Govern the Unaligned to move blood
to an uncontrolled vampire. That minion may not play Govern the
Unaligned again this turn. It may, however, play any other actions.
This includes bleeding with any card other than GtU, and it also includes
giving blood to an uncontrolled vampire with Scouting Mission.

> 2) Is the Crimson Sentinel banned?
>

The Banned list is as follows:
Cunctator Motion (V:TES)
High Stakes (V:TES)
Stake (Jyhad)
Rowan Ring (Jyhad)
Monocle of Clarity (Jyhad)
Playing for Keeps (Dark Sovereigns)
Madness of the Bard (Dark Sovereigns)

I find it odd that there are no Ancient Hearts or Sabbat cards listed...
Hmm... Anyway, Crimson Sentinel is not banned, nor do I think it should
be. Basically, the two "paralyze" cards from Jyhad are out, because
paralyzation no longer exists; Monocle of Clarity is out because it's way
too abusive; Madness of the Bard is out, because many tournament players
do not have English as a first language; and all ante cards are out,
because you are never required to play for ante in tournaments.

> 3) If I understand the stikes discussion correctly, if Basilia is
> equipped with Tiger Claws, in combat she can either strike her opponent
> for 3 normal damage or 1 ag damage. The Tiger Claws is a melee weapon
> strike, not a boost to her hand strike, thus she does not have 3 ag
> damage. Is this correct? Why was this ruling made, if correct?
>

This is correct. This is how the card always worked, and how all melee
weapons work. Basilia does not deal agg damage with a Bastard Sword,
Meat Cleaver, Bang Nakh, etc. There may have been a ruling on this, but
it was only clarification, as melee weapon damage is not and has never
been hand damage.

> 4) Camille Devereux had a name change to Raven in the V:tES reprint.
> She also apparently had a face lift (aka new artwork). Can I have one
> of each of these cards in play uncontested, or do they contest each
> other?
>

They have different names, and are thus different vampires. House rules,
such as on JOL, often say that they are the same vampire, however.

> 5) I don't understand the M1kF discussion about requirement vs.
> restriction. How does the Inner Circle member using M1kF to take over
> the Atonement action result? What are some other examples to clarify
> requirement vs. restriction?
>

I'm curious about this one myself. LSJ?

> 6) Why would the Leather Jacket not prevent the damage done by a
> vampire playing Burst of Sunlight? The Jacket prevents damage done from
> a strike, but it doesn't necessarily have to be your opponent's strike,
> does it? Same for Body of Sun at basic level - both vampires take 3 or
> 1 ag damage, depending on range. The Jacket could be used to prevent
> that damage as well, couldn't it?
>

No. I'm not real happy about this myself, but there has been made a
distinction between "damage from a strike" and damage from a side effect
of a strike. Damage from a strike has been ruled to be: damage dealt by
an opposing minion to this minion as a result of a strike card.

> 7) Where can I find the FAQs and rulings lists? I've tried searching
> dejanews, but I haven't had much luck.
>

Well, you should be able to find them on Deja News, since LSJ posts them
every month. Otherwise go to
http://www.deckserver.net/cgi-deckserver/rulemonger.cgi

-Chris

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Scott Halvorson wrote:
> Reading the newsgroups and playing with friends have raised a few
> questions that I need to know the answers to, also to explain a few
> rulings to my gaming group.
>

> 1) What is the official ruling on vampires performing the same action
> twice in a turn? I thought that it can't be done, but someone else has
> said that it depends on the cards played. For example, a vampire bleeds
> me with Social Charms, and I block it. During combat, he plays Majesty
> to end combat and untap. Then he wants to bleed me with the same
> vampire using Govern the Unaligned. I say that he can't perform a
> second bleed action. He says that he is using a different card do
> bleed, so it is allowed. What is the ruling?

The actual rules do not prohibit repeated actions at all. You are
free to Social Charm, untap and Social Charm again if you like.
The Tournament rules, however, include a "No Repeat Actions" clause,
which functions the way you say (a bleed is a bleed, Social Charm
or other card name make no difference).

Most people seem to play the Tournament Rule.

> Also, along these lines,
> Why is Obedience printed the way it is (vampire may not perform this
> action again) if the way I think the rule is is correct?

Because it applies to the non-tournament game as well (and it only
cares about the exact action, not the action type, so would allow
a Govern after a Social Charm).

> Same for
> Rutor's Hand; will it allow a tapped vampire who bled earlier to bleed
> again?

Tournament rules: no.

> 2) Is the Crimson Sentinel banned?

No.

> 3) If I understand the stikes discussion correctly, if Basilia is
> equipped with Tiger Claws, in combat she can either strike her opponent
> for 3 normal damage or 1 ag damage. The Tiger Claws is a melee weapon
> strike, not a boost to her hand strike, thus she does not have 3 ag
> damage. Is this correct? Why was this ruling made, if correct?

It is correct.
It was made because it is the way these things were intended to work.

> 4) Camille Devereux had a name change to Raven in the V:tES reprint.
> She also apparently had a face lift (aka new artwork). Can I have one
> of each of these cards in play uncontested, or do they contest each
> other?

They are distinct; you can have both in play at the same time.

> 5) I don't understand the M1kF discussion about requirement vs.
> restriction. How does the Inner Circle member using M1kF to take over
> the Atonement action result?

Assuming the IC has enough blood to pay the cost, the Atonement
resolves as normal.

> What are some other examples to clarify
> requirement vs. restriction?

Restrictions:
* Empty Ready vampires cannot take any action except "hunt"
* Minions with Talbots Chainsaw cannot hunt
* Assamites (in general) cannot commit diablerie
* Vampire with Minor Boon cannot bleed the Booning Methuselah.

Requirements:
* Inferior (as well as superior) Social Charm requires Presence
* Fifth Tradition requires a Prince/Justicar
* Covenant of Blood requires a Non-Camrilla w/ capacity > 7
* Recruiting a Renegade Garou requires a Gangrel

> 6) Why would the Leather Jacket not prevent the damage done by a
> vampire playing Burst of Sunlight? The Jacket prevents damage done from
> a strike, but it doesn't necessarily have to be your opponent's strike,
> does it? Same for Body of Sun at basic level - both vampires take 3 or
> 1 ag damage, depending on range. The Jacket could be used to prevent
> that damage as well, couldn't it?

No. "Damage from a strike" doesn't include the side-effect
(self-inflicted) damage done by a strike.

> 7) Where can I find the FAQs and rulings lists? I've tried searching
> dejanews, but I haven't had much luck.

Dejanews, search for: "~g rec.*.jyhad & ~a vtesrep* & ~s Errata"
(or replace "Errata" with "Rulings" or "Clarifications").

or go to Wizard's VTES Rules page:
http://www.wizards.com/VTES/VTES_Rules.html

--
L. Scott Johnson (vte...@wizards.com)
Official VtES Net.Rep for Wizards of the Coast.
(*) - Subject to review by Rules Team

single-backed (black) crypt.

Similarly for any other style of opaque-backed sleeves, so long as
the sleeves are uniform, before anyone asks.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Joshua Duffin wrote:
> : Of course, in tournament play, it isn't possible to play both in any
> : given deck because then you would have a mixed back crypt.
>
> Well, according to my understanding that rule is optional. (As is the
> 40-60 rule on mixed backs in the library.)
>
> If I'm wrong, please let me know, as I'm going to be running a tourney,
> and I don't plan on using either of the mixing restriction rules.

You are correct. By default, neither the uniform-back crypt nor the
40%-60% ratio library rule are used in DCI tournaments. To use
either (or both) of these rules, the tournament Officials, Organizers,
and/or Judges must give "adequate notice to participants" that the
optional rule(s) will be used.

Excerpts from the DCI Rules:

Important note regarding all optional rules: Tournament Organizers,
Tournament Officials, and Judges who choose to use any rule marked
"optional" must provide adequate notice to participants prior to the beginning
of the tournament. Optional rules may not be invoked or altered either by
Tournament Officials or players at any other time.

I. DECK CONSTRUCTION
[...]
OPTIONAL: Prior to the beginning of a sanctioned tournament, the
Judge may declare that players who build decks from cards from both
JyhadTM and Vampire: The Eternal StruggleTM sets should ensure that
between forty and sixty percent of their library be from the JyhadTM set.
[...]
OPTIONAL: The Judge may declare that players may build their
crypts with cards from either Vampire: The Eternal StruggleTM or
JyhadTM, but not both.



Actually, LSJ, I believe the DCI's position on sleeves is that the cards
inside the sleeves must be legal. This came about due to the Pro Tour
Magic decks that had different card backs which were illegal for
tournaments. Practically speaking though, no one will find out that
your deck is illegal unless the sleeves are requested to be removed.
